14	CASE OD2-HO-CHANGE-2 (CHANGE, technical): Ashgrove Heights low pressure
15	Setting: Calder Vale Water (fictional) supplies about 410,000 people through 23 district metered areas (DMAs). Each DMA is fed through a metered inlet and is normally kept separate from its neighbours by closed boundary valves. Ashgrove Heights is a hillside DMA of about 6,800 properties. It is fed through a pressure-reducing valve (PRV) on Ridgeway Road. Millbrook Low is the lower-lying DMA that adjoins it to the east. Stage S1 covers evidence available up to 15 September; stage S2 covers evidence gathered from 16 September to 5 October.
16	Presenting request: On 6 October the Director of Network Operations wants an independent diagnosis of the Ashgrove Heights pressure drop before deciding on two requests from the Network Operations Manager: book a rail possession to dig up the trunk main under the rail cutting, and raise the Ashgrove PRV setpoint to 4.8 bar in the meantime.
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Telemetry summary, critical-point logger PL-AG-03 (telemetry): Critical-point logger PL-AG-03 (Beacon Hill Road, the highest point in Ashgrove Heights DMA). 1–8 Sept: lowest morning-peak pressure (07:00–08:30) 3.1–3.2 bar; overnight 3.7 bar. 9–15 Sept: lowest morning-peak pressure 1.5–1.7 bar every day; overnight 3.0 bar. The company's service reference level is 2.0 bar at peak. Low-pressure customer contacts from Ashgrove: 4 in the whole of August, 38 between 9 and 15 Sept, clustered on Beacon Hill and Ridgeway.
19	E2 [stage S1] Ashgrove Heights DMA inlet meter extract, prepared 15 Sept (telemetry): Ashgrove Heights inlet meter (Ridgeway Road). Minimum night flow (02:00–04:00): 1–8 Sept 6.2–6.4 L/s; 10–15 Sept 14.7–14.9 L/s. One-minute data show a step at 06:40 on 9 Sept: flow rose by 8.6 L/s within four minutes and has stayed up at all hours since. Daily inflow was about 1,950 m³ before and 2,690 m³ after. Analyst comment: the 7–12 Sept heatwave raised daytime demand across the whole system, but no other DMA shows a step in night flow, and Ashgrove's higher night flow continued after temperatures fell on 13 Sept.
20	E3 [stage S1] Network works register, weeks 34–37 (extract) (change-record): 29 Aug — Fenwick Fields development, Ashgrove: the last 12 of 38 new homes connected; development complete. 5 Sept — Ashgrove inlet PRV (Ridgeway Road): annual service by in-house team, pilot valve replaced, 4.0 bar setpoint re-confirmed. 9–27 Sept — Millbrook Low DMA (adjoins Ashgrove to the east): Station Road main renewal, contractor Brannock Civils, permit PTW-2291. Standing condition on all contractor permits: supply-continuity arrangements must be agreed with network control before work starts.
21	E4 [stage S1] Ashgrove inlet PRV controller trend, 1–15 Sept, with asset note (telemetry): Ridgeway Road PRV. Inlet pressure 7.1–7.3 bar. Outlet pressure 3.97–4.03 bar throughout the period, including after the 5 Sept service and after 9 Sept. Valve opening rose from about 31% to about 44% starting at 06:40 on 9 Sept and has stayed there. Asset note on file: under pressure-management policy PM-7, the Ashgrove PRV outlet is capped at 4.2 bar. The cap was set after the 2022 burst cluster, when the outlet was raised to 4.6 bar and the district's 1960s cast-iron mains had 14 bursts in six weeks. Any setting above 4.2 bar requires an asset-risk review.
22	E5 [stage S1] Field note, network technician D. Okafor, 12 Sept (staff-account): 'Asked to rule out water crossing the boundary. GIS shows four pipe connections between Ashgrove and neighbouring DMAs: BV-21 and BV-22 to Millbrook Low, BV-23 to Castle Rise, BV-24 to Northfield. GIS says these are the only mains connections. I found all four and all were shut: I turned each spindle in the closing direction and none moved. I gauged both sides of each valve, and the pressure differences of 0.9–1.6 bar held, so they are sealing. The register agrees. I also asked network control whether any temporary cross-boundary links (including hose or hydrant links) or works cross-feeds had been agreed for Ashgrove or its neighbours; they checked and none were on record. Nothing is crossing at the boundary. My view: look for a burst.'
23	E6 [stage S2] Email, R. Halvorsen, Network Operations Manager, 30 Sept (manager-account): 'The acoustic survey has covered about 70% of Ashgrove mains and found two service-pipe leaks (about 0.4 L/s combined), repaired on 26 Sept. Minimum night flow since then is 14.6 L/s, so the big one is still out there. The only stretch not surveyed is the 1968 trunk main under the rail cutting, where we can't place loggers without a rail possession. Boundary valves were checked and ruled out, and the PRV is fine, so this is a burst under the railway. I'm asking for approval to book a possession and dig. Customer services have already texted every Beacon Hill and Ridgeway customer (16 and 29 Sept) and keep a web notice updated. Meanwhile I propose raising the PRV to 4.8 bar so Beacon Hill customers get above 2 bar at peak.'
24	CATALOGUE (full contents)
25	C1 [stage S1] Ashgrove inlet PRV service record and controller event log, 1–15 Sept - Asset maintenance system (system-record): Work order WO-58812, 5 Sept: annual service, Ridgeway Road PRV. Pilot valve replaced because of seat wear, strainer cleaned, setpoint checked at 4.0 bar against a test gauge, valve back in service 11:20. Controller event log 1–15 Sept: no alarms, no setpoint changes, no manual overrides. One informational event (not alarmed) on 9 Sept at 06:41: 'valve position increase >10% in 5 min'. Technician comment: 'Valve moving smoothly, outlet steady.'
26	C2 [stage S2] Acoustic leak survey crew sheets, Ashgrove, 16–27 Sept - Leakage team (log): Noise loggers placed in five rounds across 14.2 km of Ashgrove mains, about 70% of total length. Correlated noise found at two places: 14 Ridgeway Close (service pipe, estimated 0.25 L/s) and 3 Orchard Mews (service pipe, estimated 0.15 L/s). Both repaired 26 Sept. All other loggers were quiet. Section RC (1968 trunk main under the rail cutting, 0.6 km) was not surveyed because the fittings cannot be reached safely without a rail possession. Crew note: 'What we've covered doesn't look like a typical burst.'
27	C3 [stage S1] Fenwick Fields new-connection schedule and occupancy, July–Sept - New connections team (system-record): Fenwick Fields, 38 homes. Connected: 14 in July, 12 on 8 Aug, 12 on 29 Aug. The developer reported 31 of 38 occupied at 15 Sept. Design allowance for night demand is 0.05 L/s on average for all 38 homes combined. Meters are fitted at every property; first readings are due in December.
28	C4 [stage S2] Millbrook Low DMA inlet flow and pressure telemetry, 1 Aug–30 Sept - Telemetry historian (telemetry): Millbrook Low inlet PRV setpoint 3.0 bar. Minimum night flow 1 Aug–8 Sept: 10.7–11.1 L/s. From 9 Sept: 2.4–2.7 L/s. One-minute data show the fall starting at 06:38 on 9 Sept and finished by 06:44. Daily inflow fell from about 3,110 m³ to about 2,385 m³. No change around 27 Sept. Millbrook critical-point pressures stayed in their normal range throughout. Ashgrove and Millbrook inflows combined: 5,060 m³/day on average for 1–8 Sept, 5,075 m³/day on average for 9–30 Sept (meter uncertainty about ±2%).
29	C5 [stage S2] Station Road main renewal (PTW-2291): method statement, permit and contractor site diary - Permit office file, Brannock Civils documents (document): Method statement §4: 'Isolating the Station Road main removes the main feed to east Millbrook. To hold pressure, run a temporary 80 mm overland hose from hydrant AG-417, Kestrel Road (Ashgrove side, higher pressure), to hydrant ML-112, Station Road east. Remove on recommissioning.' Diary, 9 Sept early shift: 'Main isolated. Overland link charged from AG-417; east Millbrook holding. Rang control about the link — ok'd.' Diary, 27 Sept: 'New main flushed, sampled, recommissioned. Millbrook back on its own feed.' Diary, 3 Oct: 'Overland link still connected, waiting for hose crew.' Permit §7 ('network control agreement: name/time') is blank. Permit officer note: §7 is normally completed at close-out, and this permit is still open; the 9 Sept diary entries were written up on 4 Oct, after the Ashgrove investigation contacted Brannock.
30	C6 [stage S1] Boundary valve register and field check sheets, Ashgrove, March and 12 Sept - Network records (document): Register: BV-21 and BV-22 (Ashgrove–Millbrook Low), BV-23 (Ashgrove–Castle Rise), BV-24 (Ashgrove–Northfield). All have status 'closed – normally shut', last verified 14 March. Check sheets, 12 Sept (D. Okafor): each valve located, spindle tried in the closing direction, no turns available. Pressure difference across each valve: BV-21 1.1 bar, BV-22 0.9 bar, BV-23 1.6 bar, BV-24 1.3 bar. GIS note: 'No other mains connections between these DMAs.' Register updated to 'verified 12 Sept'.
31	C7 [stage S1] Smart-meter sample of Ashgrove household night use, Aug–15 Sept - Customer metering analytics (system-record): Sample of 120 Ashgrove households with half-hourly smart meters, excluding Fenwick Fields. Average household use 02:00–04:00: August 1.9 L/h; 1–8 Sept 2.0 L/h; 9–15 Sept 2.0 L/h. Average daytime use rose about 11% during 7–12 Sept and was back to August levels by 14 Sept. No household in the sample shows a lasting rise in night use above 20 L/h.
32	C8 [stage S2] Control room shift log and call-recorder status, 8–10 Sept - Network control (log): Shift log, 9 Sept: Northfield 300 mm burst reported at 05:52. From 05:52 to 09:30 the entries cover only Northfield (valving, tanker requests, customer messages). No entry mentions Station Road, Brannock Civils or Millbrook between 05:00 and 12:00. IT notice: the call-recording platform was offline from 8 Sept 22:00 to 10 Sept 14:00 for a migration; incoming calls were connected but not recorded. The early-shift duty controller on 9 Sept is on extended leave until 20 Oct and has not been interviewed.
33	C9 [stage S1] Beacon Hill pressure logger calibration and handheld cross-check - Metering team (independent-observation): Logger PL-AG-03 calibrated 11 June, error +0.02 bar. Handheld gauge cross-check at the hydrant next to it, 13 Sept 07:35: handheld 1.62 bar, logger 1.65 bar. Second check, 13 Sept 02:30: handheld 3.02 bar, logger 3.04 bar. No faults recorded on the logger since installation.
34	C10 [stage S1] Asset record: Ashgrove trunk main section RC (rail cutting) - Asset register (document): Section RC: 0.6 km of 300 mm cast iron laid in 1968, running under the rail cutting between Kestrel Road and Ridgeway. Recorded failures: a circumferential break in 2019 (repaired under a rail possession that took 11 days to schedule) and a joint leak in 2021. Condition grade 4 of 5. Asset planner note, 2024: 'High consequence, poor access; candidate for renewal next investment period.'
35	C11 [stage S2] Millbrook Low customer contacts log, 1–30 Sept - Customer contact system (system-record): 9 Sept, 06:02–06:31: nine contacts from Station Road east and Weir Lane reporting 'no water' or 'very low pressure'. 9 Sept, 06:50: one contact, 'water back, a bit cloudy'. No further pressure contacts from Millbrook in September. Discoloured-water contacts: two on 27 Sept (Station Road). Note: planned-works letters for Station Road had been sent on 2 Sept.
36	C12 [stage S1] Weather and system demand summary, 1–15 Sept - Demand planning (external-data): Maximum temperatures 29–33 °C on 7–12 Sept and 21–23 °C from 13 Sept. System-wide daily demand was 9% higher on 7–12 Sept than on 1–6 Sept and back to baseline by 14 Sept. Minimum night flows in the 22 other DMAs moved by no more than ±0.4 L/s over 1–15 Sept. Four elevated DMAs had peak-hour pressure dips of 0.2–0.4 bar during the heat; all had recovered by 13 Sept.
37	C13 [stage S2] Hydraulic model study of Ashgrove pressure loss scenarios, 1 Oct - Merrow Hydraulics (consultant), commissioned by Network Operations (expert-account): Brief: 'locate likely burst'. Two scenarios were run, each with 8.6 L/s outflow: one at node RC-3 (rail cutting) and one at node BH-7 (Beacon Hill). RC-3 matches observed Beacon Hill peak and night pressures to within 0.15 bar; BH-7 overstates the night drop by 0.5 bar. Conclusion: 'Observed pressures are consistent with a burst of about 8.6 L/s on section RC.' Limitations: scenarios were limited to the brief, and outflows at other nodes in the downstream half of the network were not tested.
38	C14 [stage S2] Rail possession quotation and excavation plan, section RC - Network Operations / rail operator (financial-record): Rail operator quotation: three overnight possessions, earliest 4–6 Nov, £61,000. Civils estimate for excavation, traffic management on Kestrel Road and reinstatement: £23,500. Total £84,500. The plan assumes the leak is within ±50 m of node RC-3, as indicated by the model study. If nothing is found, a second possession window would be needed, earliest in January.
39	C15 [stage S2] Ashgrove inlet meter in-situ verification, 24 Sept - Metering team (independent-observation): Insertion-probe comparison, 24 Sept 01:30–04:30. Permanent meter average 14.7 L/s; insertion probe 14.5 L/s. The 1.4% difference is within the ±2% tolerance. The meter was last verified in February, and its configuration has not changed since it was installed in 2020.
40	CANDIDATES
41	H1: A leak or burst on mains within Ashgrove Heights, downstream of the district inlet meter, is losing water and causing the pressure drop.
42	H2: The Ashgrove inlet pressure-reducing valve is delivering less outlet pressure than its setpoint, causing the pressure drop.
43	H3: Water is passing out of Ashgrove Heights into a neighbouring district's network, causing the pressure drop.
44	H4: Higher customer demand within Ashgrove Heights is drawing the district's pressure down.
45	H5: The Station Road contractor did not inform network control of the supply-continuity arrangements it made for its works.
46	R1: Station Road main renewal works in Millbrook Low (from 9 Sept) -> Ashgrove Heights pressure drop from 9 Sept (causes)
47	R2: Ashgrove inlet PRV service and pilot-valve replacement on 5 Sept -> Ashgrove Heights pressure drop from 9 Sept (causes)
48	R3: Fenwick Fields new-home connections -> 9 Sept step rise in Ashgrove minimum night flow (causes)
49	A1: Find and remove any temporary connection between Ashgrove and Millbrook, once Millbrook's Station Road main is confirmed back in service, then check both district meters and the Beacon Hill logger for recovery.
50	A2: Raise the Ashgrove inlet PRV setpoint from 4.0 to 4.8 bar now, to bring Beacon Hill customers back above 2 bar at peak.
51	A3: Issue the Station Road contractor a formal non-conformance for not informing network control of its supply-continuity arrangements.
52	A4: Send a further letter to affected Beacon Hill and Ridgeway customers explaining the low-pressure problem and that a fix is being worked on.
53	SCORED ITEMS

55	S02: hypothesis H1 asOfStage=S1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
56	S03: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
57	S04: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
58	S05: hypothesis H3 asOfStage=S1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
59	S06: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
60	S07: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
61	S08: edge R1 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
62	S09: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
63	S10: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
64	S11: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
65	S12: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
66	S13: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
67	S14: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
68	S15: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]

answers.justification: Ashgrove and Millbrook inflows together stayed flat (5,060 vs 5,075 m³/day, C4) while Ashgrove rose and Millbrook fell by the same amount within the same minutes (E2, C4). That means the extra water went into Millbrook's network, not out of an Ashgrove main. The acoustic survey also found only 0.4 L/s of leaks (C2), and the model never tested other draw-off points (C13).

At S1, a sustained 8.6 L/s step with no rise in household use (C7, C12), a steady PRV (E4, C1) and closed boundary valves (E5, C6) points toward a burst. However, the Station Road works next door started the same day (E3), and the boundary check only covered recorded links (E5), so a transfer into Millbrook was still an equally live rival.
PRV outlet pressure held at 3.97–4.03 bar throughout, including after 9 Sept, while the valve opened further to pass more flow (E4). The controller log shows no alarms or setpoint changes (C1).

The method statement and site diary describe an 80 mm overland hose from Ashgrove hydrant AG-417 to Millbrook, charged on 9 Sept and still connected on 3 Oct (C5). Millbrook inflow fell by about 8.4 L/s at 06:38–06:44 as Ashgrove's rose 8.6 L/s at 06:40 (C4, E2), the combined inflow balanced (C4), and Millbrook's no-water calls stopped by 06:50 (C11).

At S1 the boundary valves were sealing and network control had no recorded cross-feeds (E5, C6). That check could not rule out an unrecorded link, and the adjoining Millbrook works began on the day of the step (E3), so H3 was live but unestablished.

Smart-meter household night use stayed at 2.0 L/h (C7). The heatwave raised only daytime demand and left night flows in the other DMAs within ±0.4 L/s (C12, E2), and Ashgrove's raised flow continued after the heat ended (E2).

Control had no record of the link and the shift log never mentions it (E5, C8). But control was taken up with the Northfield burst, calls were not being recorded, the duty controller has not been interviewed (C8), and the diary's claim that control 'ok'd' the link was written up after the fact (C5). The evidence does not settle the question either way.

The timing matches to the minute (C4, E2, C5, C11). There is a clear mechanism: a hose from AG-417 feeding Millbrook (C5). The two meters move in opposite directions while the combined inflow stays flat (C4), which rules out the main rival, a burst inside Ashgrove.
The service was on 5 Sept but the drop began on 9 Sept (E1, E2). The outlet held its 4.0 bar setpoint the whole time, with no alarms or overrides logged (E4, C1).
Fenwick Fields was fully connected by 29 Aug, well before the 9 Sept step (C3, E3), and its design night demand is only 0.05 L/s against an 8.6 L/s step (C3).

Removing the documented hose link (C5) after confirming the Station Road main is back in service (C5 diary, 27 Sept) treats the most likely cause. Checking both district meters and the Beacon Hill logger afterwards will confirm or rule out H3 cheaply, before the £84,500 possession is booked (C14).

A setting of 4.8 bar breaks the PM-7 cap of 4.2 bar, which was set after 14 cast-iron bursts at 4.6 bar (E4). It would push even more water through the link into Millbrook (C5) without fixing the cause.

Whether the contractor failed to tell control is unresolved: the diary claims control 'ok'd' the link, the call recorder was offline and the duty controller has not been interviewed (C5, C8). A non-conformance now could penalise the wrong party.
Customers were already texted on 16 and 29 Sept and a web notice is kept updated (E6), so another letter is reasonable but adds little and is not among the best next actions.

The flat combined inflow (C4), the documented and still-connected hose link (C5) and the matching timing (E2, C11) are enough to justify removing the link (A1). The decision is low-risk and reversible, and recovery checks will verify it.
